subject: geography

moments.title: IPCC established
moments.body: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change is established by the World Meteorological Organization and UN Environment Programme. It does no original research; it synthesises peer-reviewed work into Assessment Reports.
moments.takeaway: The IPCC structure — intergovernmental, with line-by-line approval of the Summary for Policymakers — gives the conclusions political weight and limits how strongly they can be stated.

moments.title: Five Assessment Reports
moments.body: FAR (1990): broad warning, basis for the UNFCCC. SAR (1995): 'discernible human influence'. TAR (2001): 'most of the observed warming over the last 50 years is likely to have been due to the increase in greenhouse gas concentrations'. AR4 (2007): Nobel Peace Prize with Al Gore. AR5 (2014): basis for the Paris Agreement.
moments.takeaway: Each Report has strengthened the human attribution. Confidence language has shifted from 'likely' to 'extremely likely' and 'unequivocal'.

moments.title: AR6
moments.who: Working Groups I, II and III
moments.body: AR6: 'It is unequivocal that human influence has warmed the atmosphere, ocean and land'. Sea level projections, tipping point assessment, mitigation pathways, including 1.5 °C scenarios. The Synthesis Report (March 2023) is the most uncompromising IPCC framing yet.

quote.text: It is unequivocal that human influence has warmed the atmosphere, ocean and land.

moments.takeaway: AR6 was widely reported as a 'code red for humanity' (UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres).

now.title: Synthesis under pressure
now.body: AR7 cycle is underway, expected by 2029. The IPCC's strength — consensus by governments — is also its weakness, as oil-producing states have blocked stronger language in some Summary documents. Independent assessments (Climate Action Tracker, World Resources Institute) sometimes go further.
now.open_questions: Can a consensus body keep pace with accelerating change? Some scientists argue for parallel rapid assessments that don't need intergovernmental approval.

reflection: The IPCC is one of the most successful experiments in transnational scientific assessment. Its caution is structural and intentional — and its conclusions are now alarming enough that even cautious language reshapes politics.
